title: Safeguarding Elections Act
lastAction: Ref To Com On Rules, Calendar, and Operations of the House
aiSummary: This bill makes multiple changes to North Carolina election laws. It prohibits armed forces at polling places, creates new criminal penalties for voter intimidation and coercion, establishes protections for election workers, adjusts early voting hours, disqualifies officials who refuse to certify elections, restricts certain post-election audits, regulates poll observers, protects voter privacy, extends voter challenge deadlines, and requires notice to voters whose absentee ballots are challenged.
aiProArguments: Supporters argue this bill strengthens election security and protects democratic processes by preventing intimidation of voters and election workers, ensuring election officials certify accurate results, establishing uniform audit procedures conducted by nonpartisan experts, and protecting voter privacy. They contend it safeguards voters' ability to cast ballots under the rules in place when they vote and prevents last-minute legal challenges that could disenfranchise voters who followed established procedures.
aiConArguments: Opponents may argue the bill creates overly broad definitions of voter intimidation and election interference that could chill legitimate political speech and observation activities, that disqualifying officials for refusing to certify elections removes important checks on certification procedures, that restricting certain audits limits legitimate election transparency efforts, and that extending challenge deadlines and new litigation procedures could complicate election administration and create additional litigation opportunities.
